## Fix: Create Base in the migration dialog

In 0.5.2, **Create Base** could look enabled after the review but ignore clicks. The dialog updated the HTML disabled attribute without updating Obsidian's ButtonComponent state.

**0.5.3 fixes the control state** after the initial review, Refresh review, creation attempts and errors. The button now creates and opens the Base through the existing migration flow.

If you installed 0.5.2, update the same plugin with `main.js`, `manifest.json` and `styles.css` below, reload it, and reopen **Create Bases planner**. Keep `data.json` and your notes. Existing Base files do not need to be migrated again.

The review also refreshes its cached membership when classic discovery resumes, excluding notes that were removed from the planner while it was paused. This prevents a stale count from blocking the initial migration comparison.

The classic view remains available during the transition, with no removal date set. Migration creates a new Base without moving, renaming or rewriting the original notes/settings.

[Migration guide](https://github.com/DavidHurtadoAI/just-simple-planner/blob/0.5.3/docs/MIGRATION.md) · [Guía en español](https://github.com/DavidHurtadoAI/just-simple-planner/blob/0.5.3/docs/MIGRACION.es.md) · [0.5.2 features and screenshots](https://github.com/DavidHurtadoAI/just-simple-planner/releases/tag/0.5.2)

Validation: 63 unit tests, strict TypeScript, official lint with zero warnings, production/package checks, eight in-app scenarios that activate the actual migration controls, and the 24 existing Bases integration checks. The UI scenarios cover the classic banner, the command with no classic view open, Refresh review, duplicate/invalid paths with retry, changed notes requiring a fresh review, and repeated clicks. Original note bytes, classic settings and the workspace layout are retained. GitHub Actions builds and verifies provenance for all three release files.
